methodological_rigor.justification: Case series of 9 biliary neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) patients with literature review. No control group; no comparative analysis. Small sample (n=9) precludes multivariate analysis, acknowledged by authors. Data presented descriptively without statistical testing. Literature review provides context but does not strengthen case series rigor. Retrospective data collection with variable completeness across cases (incomplete chemotherapy regimen details). No power calculation or formal hypothesis testing.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series reporting clinicopathological characteristics and treatment outcomes of rare malignancy (LoE 4). Clinical relevance high for rare disease recognition and management guidance, but low level of evidence. No randomized comparison of treatments; observations descriptive rather than conclusive regarding optimal therapy. Potential value for clinician awareness of diagnostic features and survival outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: Adequate case-by-case data reporting with clinical characteristics, imaging, pathology, treatment, and outcomes. Immunohistochemistry findings detailed with representative images. However, incomplete reporting of chemotherapy regimens and cycles; missing data acknowledged as limitation. No data availability statement. Case series lacks structured reporting framework (CARE guidelines not mentioned).

novelty_literature.justification: Documentation of rare biliary NEC cases; literature review summarizes 15 prior reports (17 patients total). Incremental contribution to understanding of this extremely rare malignancy (0.5% of neuroendocrine neoplasms). No novel mechanistic insights; findings consistent with prior reports. Ki-67 and lymph node metastasis identified as prognostic factors (previously recognized). Chemotherapy association with survival benefit noted but not definitively established in this small series.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear presentation of case series with well-organized clinical summaries and comprehensive pathological descriptions. Literature review effectively contextualizes findings. Discussion acknowledges limitations transparently and identifies gaps in knowledge (molecular profiling, immunogenomic analysis). Figures illustrate histopathology and clinical course effectively. Limitations section appropriately detailed regarding small sample size and incomplete data.

key_strengths: Comprehensive case documentation of rare malignancy with detailed pathological and immunohistochemical analysis (Syn, CgA, CD56, Ki-67)
Literature review synthesis (26 additional patients) provides context and identifies consistent prognostic factors (Ki-67 index, lymph node metastasis)
Clear description of surgical approaches (R0 resection rate 89%) and treatment outcomes; median OS 21 months reported with individual case timelines
Transparent acknowledgment of limitations and call for multicenter studies with molecular profiling
key_concerns: Very small sample size (n=9) severely limits statistical power; multivariate analysis impossible; observations descriptive only
No control arm or comparative analysis; cannot establish treatment efficacy or prognostic factor significance beyond descriptive observation
Incomplete chemotherapy data for some cases; treatment decisions not standardized; selection bias regarding which patients received chemotherapy
High mortality despite R0 resection (89%) suggests aggressive biology, but lack of control makes causal inferences impossible
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 4 case series appropriate for rare disease documentation. Small sample and descriptive nature limit evidence level. Suitable for publication but requires managing expectations about generalizability and statistical conclusions.
